newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Bullish Australian stocks soar to record close.
newsitem.headline: Bullish Australian stocks soar to record close.

text.p: A bullish Australian share market bolted above the 2,600 level for the first time ever on Friday, shattering turnover milestones and previous records on the way.
The All Ordinaries index soared 19.9 points to a record closing level of 2,610.5, having touched a record high of 2,617.4, easily surpassing Thursday's record high of 2,591.5.
The hat trick of records was completed by an impressive, albeit options-boosted, A$1.88 billion (US$1.43 billion) turnover. The previous record turnover was A$1.74 billion on December 20, 1996.
"It's been a fantastic market, particularly BHP," said Grant Williams, dealer at brokerage Reynolds and Co, although he noted gains were widespread with healthy buying interest apparent.
"But other things like ANZ have carried it along as well. There seems to be quite a demand for good stocks at the moment."

BHP posted a gain of 1.4 percent to close at A$18.86 still recovering from its sharp selldown after Monday's fourth quarter profit warning, and aided by the resetting of positions after Thursday's May option expiries.
"Given the options expiry yesterday, there may well have been some short covering today," Williams said.
Others concurred, although they said other factors had also boosted the bellwether stock.

"They are running ahead on some of their new projects and I think the market has factored that in, plus it always helps if you have a little oil discovery as well," said Daiwa Securities dealer, Mark Pervan, noting Thursday's Algerian oil find.
ANZ Bank was the strongest performer in the banks, adding three percent to A$8.99, while National Australia Bank ended 1.2 percent up at A$18.78.

It was not all rosy for all of the big four though, with Westpac and Commonwealth Bank largely ignored. Westpac ended just a cent higher at A$7.13 after spending most of the day below square, while Commonwealth Bank fell victim to an afternoon ambush by sellers who slashed 1.8 percent off the stock to A$14.12 by the close.
Brokers cited switching to the more attractive ANZ Bank and National Australia Bank, as well as quality of earnings issues.
"ANZ's result compared to Westpac just shows up the difference between the two," said Reynolds' Williams.
Chemicals group ICI Australia just firmed to A$12.15 after announcing a A$360 million buyback of parent ICI Plc's stake.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about nine to five, while about 27 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
